critical_code_review_comments: workflow add-data uses Windows-style separator 'yolov8n.pt;.' which is correct because runner is windows-latest (PyInstaller uses ';' on Windows, ':' on Linux). OK.

Release step uses tag_name v${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }} which will produce tag v1.0.0. If the workflow is triggered by pushing an existing v1.0.0 tag, softprops/action-gh-release will update/replace it; if bumping APP_VERSION, the corresponding tag must be pushed OR the action will create it on the current commit. Consider gating the Release step with `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` to avoid creating releases on every main-branch push.
Consider adding an actions/cache step for the PyInstaller build (`build/` and `dist/`) to speed up subsequent runs, though not required for correctness.
The 90-minute timeout is generous; a first-time run with torch+easyocr onefile packaging typically finishes in 25-45 min, so this is safe.

rca_of_the_issue: Original 'stuck at font cache' was a false alarm - PyInstaller onefile archiving of torch/easyocr (~1.5 GB) runs quiet for 10-25 min. Fix in workflow addresses it correctly via: (1) explicit timeout-minutes: 90 so job doesn't get killed at the default 6h ceiling but also has a firm bound, (2) pre-building matplotlib font cache so the log line no longer appears during the quiet phase (removes the misleading 'stuck' impression), (3) --exclude-module for tkinter/IPython/pytest/notebook to shrink bundle, (4) --collect-data ultralytics easyocr to include their data files, (5) pip cache to speed reruns. All validated statically.
